textbookText: 8. How does worker bees form a new queen bee?
Ans:- By feeding a selected larva with royal jelly continuously workers bees form a new queen bee.
9. If the queen bee dies for some reason, who will control the hive?
W10. What is the process called in which a drone is developed from an unfertilized egg.
Ans:- The process called in which a drone is developed from an unfertilized egg is Parthenogenesis.
Section C
Short answer type questions
1. Write two differences between worker bee and drone bee.
Ans:- Two differences between worker bee and drone bee are
Worker Bee
Drone Bee
Worker bee has 32 chromosomes.
Drone bee has 16 chromosomes.
Worker bee collects nectar, pollen, builds hive.
Drone bee only fertilizes queen.
2. Write two differences between queens bee and worker bee.
Ans:-Two differences between worker bee and drone bee are
Queen Bee
Worker Bee
Queen bee lays eggs.
Worker bee cannot lay eggs (normally sterile).
Queen bee is larger in size.
Worker bee is smaller in size.
3. Why it is necessary to study the life cycle of the honeybee? Clarify with two reasons.
Ans:- Two reasons to study the life cycle of the honey bee are
a) To understand reproduction and colony formation.
b) To improve beekeeping and honey production.
4. In which time does the nuptial flight occur in the life cycle of honey ben? Why does it happen?
Ans:- Nuptial flight occurs when the queen becomes sexually mature (5–10 days old). It happens for mating with drones to
store sperm for life.
5. Why is honey bee called a useful insect? Give two reasons.
Ans:- Honey bee called a useful insect because
a) It produces honey and wax.
b) It helps in pollination of crops.
6. Pasture land is required for bee farming. Why?
Ans:- Pasture land provides flowers for nectar and pollen, which are food sources for bees.
7. Drone dies after mating. Why?
Ans:- Drone dies after mating because its reproductive organ gets detached inside the queen during mating.
8. How does the queen bee control other members of the have?
Ans:-The queen bee control other members of the have by releasing pheromones that regulate activities and suppress ovary
development of workers.
9. How does honey bee encourage human beings in various social behaviors? Give two reasons.
Ans:- Honey bee encourage human beings by following social behaviors.
a) By showing division of labor and cooperation in colony.
b) By teaching discipline and hard work.
10. Due to the problem of pasture land in the beekeeping area, beekeepers shifted the bees from there. After that, there was
reduction in the yield of mustard crops of nearby farmers. Based on this, explain the relationship between beekeeping and
agricultural production.
Ans:- The relationship between beekeeping and agricultural production are,
a) Bees help in pollination, which increases crop yield.
b) Without bees, pollination is reduced, leading to low mustard production.
Section 'D'
Long answer type questions.
1. Explain the life cycle of honey bee with diagram.
Ans:- Egg Stage: The life cycle of a honey bee begins when the queen bee lays eggs in the brood cells of the hive. The eggs
are very small, white, and oval in shape. Fertilized eggs develop into queens and worker bees, while unfertilized eggs
develop into drones. The egg stage lasts for about three days before hatching.
Larva Stage: After hatching, the honey bee enters the larval stage. The larvae are white, worm-like, and legless. For the first
three days, they are fed royal jelly secreted by worker bees. Later, worker and drone larvae are fed pollen and honey, while a
future queen larva continues to receive only royal jelly. This stage lasts for about five to six days, during which the larva
grows rapidly.
